# IDEAL Thinkers

> A free AI literacy and fluency curriculum for primary schools in England, Year 1 to Year 6, by Mark Anderson FCCT (ictevangelist.com). 36 lessons, six per year group, each with a lesson plan and slides. Unplugged first: every lesson can be taught without pupil devices, and pupils never need AI accounts. Licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: free for schools and teachers, not for commercial use. Credit: "IDEAL Thinkers by Mark Anderson, ictevangelist.com".

IDEAL Thinkers is the AI Literacy strand of the Primary Digital Cognition Curriculum from The EdTech Playbook. Pupils' learning builds in five progression strands (how AI works; staying in charge; safe, fair and honest; learning well; design and create). The IDEAL habits (Informed, Deliberate, Ethical, Accurate, Learning) are how pupils use AI well, with Learning Well (Try it first; Hint, not answer; Plan, use, prove) as the taught form of the L habit. The AI Loop (Learn, Spot, Guess, Check) is a simple model of how AI that learns from examples works.

## Year 1: Machines That Guess (ages 5-6)
Big question: Can a machine make a guess? [Unit overview](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-1/)
- [Lesson 1: Does it guess?](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-1/does-it-guess/): Some machines do the same thing every time. Others make guesses, and many of those use AI.
- [Lesson 2: Teaching Bleep](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-1/teaching-bleep/): AI learns from lots of examples.
- [Lesson 3: The Mystery Rule](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-1/the-mystery-rule/): AI spots patterns, then guesses. Meet the AI Loop.
- [Lesson 4: Why did it show me that?](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-1/why-did-it-show-me-that/): Some AI chooses what we see next, and we can choose on purpose.
- [Lesson 5: Picture this](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-1/picture-this/): AI can make pictures from our words, but people choose the words, and we say who made each picture.
- [Lesson 6: Boss of the Bot](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-1/boss-of-the-bot/): People make AI, and people should stay in charge of it.

## Year 2: Using AI Wisely (ages 6-7)
Big question: How do we stay in charge of AI? [Unit overview](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-2/)
- [Lesson 1: Check it!](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-2/check-it/): AI guesses can be wrong, so people check.
- [Lesson 2: Missing examples](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-2/missing-examples/): When examples are missing, AI gets things wrong for some people and things.
- [Lesson 3: Try it first](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-2/try-it-first/): My brain grows when I do the hard thinking.
- [Lesson 4: Keep it to yourself](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-2/keep-it-to-yourself/): Some things we never tell a machine.
- [Lesson 5: AI Helpers Hall of Fame](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-2/ai-helpers-hall-of-fame/): AI helps people in homes, hospitals, farms and streets.
- [Lesson 6: Bleep's Big Day Out](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-2/bleeps-big-day-out/): We stay in charge of AI: check its guesses, keep things private, think first.

## Year 3: AI in Everyday Life (ages 7-8)
Big question: Where is AI in my life, and is it helping? [Unit overview](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-3/)
- [Lesson 1: What's in your feed?](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-3/whats-in-your-feed/): Apps learn from what we do, then choose what we see.
- [Lesson 2: Is it always listening?](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-3/is-it-always-listening/): Voice assistants listen for a wake word, then record and send what we say.
- [Lesson 3: AI that helps everyone](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-3/ai-that-helps-everyone/): AI can open doors for people who see, hear or speak differently.
- [Lesson 4: Hint, not answer](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-3/hint-not-answer/): The best help makes you think.
- [Lesson 5: Who made it?](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-3/who-made-it/): Being honest about when AI has helped.
- [Lesson 6: The Helpful Feed](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-3/the-helpful-feed/): Technology for children should explain its choices, label AI and keep data private.

## Year 4: Machines That Talk (ages 8-9)
Big question: Do chatbots know what they are saying? [Unit overview](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-4/)
- [Lesson 1: What comes next?](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-4/what-comes-next/): Chatbots build answers by predicting likely next words, one at a time, from patterns in text.
- [Lesson 2: Is a chatbot a friend?](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-4/is-a-chatbot-a-friend/): Chatbots can sound friendly but do not know or care about you.
- [Lesson 3: Sure isn't right](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-4/sure-isnt-right/): Chatbots can sound certain and still be wrong.
- [Lesson 4: Ask it better](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-4/ask-it-better/): What you ask shapes what you get.
- [Lesson 5: How sure is it?](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-4/how-sure-is-it/): AI works out what is most likely from patterns, and most likely is not the same as certain.
- [Lesson 6: Chatty's Rulebook](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-4/chattys-rulebook/): People decide how chatbots behave.

## Year 5: Data, Training and Fairness (ages 9-10)
Big question: Where does AI learn from, is it fair, and how do we learn well with it? [Unit overview](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-5/)
- [Lesson 1: Rules or examples?](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-5/rules-or-examples/): Some programs follow rules people write; machine learning finds its own patterns in examples.
- [Lesson 2: Train the sorter](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-5/train-the-sorter/): AI is trained on one set of data and tested on another.
- [Lesson 3: Whose is it anyway?](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-5/whose-is-it-anyway/): Training data comes from people's work and lives, so permission matters.
- [Lesson 4: The Welcome Bot](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-5/the-welcome-bot/): Unbalanced data can lead to unfair results.
- [Lesson 5: Climb the STAIR](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-5/climb-the-stair/): Using AI to help you learn, not to learn for you.
- [Lesson 6: Train a class model](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-5/train-a-class-model/): A model is only as good as its data, so we test it and improve it.

## Year 6: AI, Society and the Future (ages 10-11)
Big question: Who decides how AI is used? [Unit overview](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-6/)
- [Lesson 1: Real or generated?](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-6/real-or-generated/): AI can fake images, voices and video, so we need a checking routine and firm rules about real people.
- [Lesson 2: Who's missing from the picture?](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-6/whos-missing-from-the-picture/): AI can repeat and magnify the patterns, and the unfairness, in its data.
- [Lesson 3: AI at work](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-6/ai-at-work/): AI is changing jobs, and some things stay human.
- [Lesson 4: Is it worth it?](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-6/is-it-worth-it/): AI uses energy, water and materials, and can also help the planet, so we decide when it is worth the cost.
- [Lesson 5: Who's responsible?](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-6/whos-responsible/): When AI makes a decision, people must be able to explain it and answer for it.
- [Lesson 6: AI for Good Design Studio](https://ailiteracycurriculum.ictevangelist.com/year-6/ai-for-good-design-studio/): Good AI starts with a real problem and real people.
